question: After the destructive ordering is fixed, should this update transaction become part of the accepted Claws lifecycle, including leaving newly installed artifacts present when a later workspace reconciliation fails?
rationale: The mechanical file-loss defect is resolvable, but the open RFC explicitly reserves acceptance of lifecycle, compatibility, and partial-update semantics for maintainers.

options.title: Fix and restack
options.body: Make workspace replacement non-destructive on failure, approve the partial-artifact recovery contract, and restack onto accepted prerequisites.

options.title: Keep prototype-only
options.body: Retain the draft as implementation evidence while the RFC and prerequisite contracts continue evolving.

options.title: Redesign the transaction
options.body: Replace this update model if maintainers do not accept core-managed artifact and workspace reconciliation with partial external mutations.

recommendation.title: Fix and restack
recommendation.body: Make workspace replacement non-destructive on failure, approve the partial-artifact recovery contract, and restack onto accepted prerequisites.
